\(2(C_{51}H_{98}O_6) + 145\ O_2 \to 102\ CO_2 + 98\ H_2O + \text{energy}\)
The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of a biomolecule used for respiration, as per the above equation would be :
solution: \(R.Q = \dfrac{\text{Volume of } CO_2 \text{ evolved}}{\text{Volume of } O_2 \text{ consumed}}\). As per the given equation, \(2(C_{51}H_{98}O_6) + 145\ O_2 \to 102\ CO_2 + 98\ H_2O + \text{Energy}\). Hence the RQ can be calculated as, \(R.Q = \dfrac{102}{145} = 0.7\). This value lies between 0.5 and 0.95.
